Mark the student's response to a question from the 2019 NSW HSC Ancient History exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Question 29 (b) [25 marks]: Assess the significance of Pompey’s extraordinary commands to developments in the late Republic.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 25):
21–25 marks: Demonstrates perceptive judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates extensive and accurate historical knowledge and understanding relevant to the question | Supports the response with interpretation and well-selected evidence from relevant sources; may analyse and evaluate sources | Communicates ideas and information in a sustained, logical and cohesive response using appropriate historical terms and concepts

11–15 marks: Demonstrates some judgement relevant to the question | Demonstrates sound historical knowledge and understanding | Supports the response with interpretation and/or evidence | Presents a logical response using some historical terms and concepts
6–10 marks: Demonstrates some knowledge relevant to the question | May use evidence from relevant sources | Communicates using some appropriate historical terms and concepts
1–5 marks: Makes general statements | May refer to source(s) | May use some historical terms and concepts
